bibliographic.title: Synthesis and Characterization of Strontium Doped Barium Titanates using Neutron Diffraction Technique

bibliographic.abstract: In the present study, structural changes due to gradual doping of Sr in BaTiO3 were investigated by both x-ray and neutron powder diffraction techniques. Ba1-xSrxTiO3(x=0.0, 0.5 and 1.0) samples were synthesized by PVA evaporation method and purity was confirmed by x-ray diffraction experiment. After that, neutron diffraction experiments were carried out and diffraction data were analyzed by Rietveld least-square data refinement method using the computer program RIETAN-2000 and FullProf to determine various crystallographic structural parameters. The cation and anion position coordinates were also determined from the data refinement method which confirmed that Ba and Sr atoms possess tetrahedral A site and Ti atoms possess octahedral B site for all three samples BaTiO3, Ba0.5Sr0.5TiO3, and SrTiO3, respectively. Moreover, the lattice parameter values indicate, Ba1-xSrxTiO3 structure undergoes a phase transition from tetragonal to cubic somewhere before x=0.5. The concurrences between observed and calculated profiles were excellent and well consistent with the previously reported values. Furthermore, MEM based analysis was done for charge density measurement.

datasets.dataset_description: XRD patterns recorded using a Phillips PW 3040 X'Pert Pro diffractometer with Cu(Kα) radiation (wavelength 1.54178 Å) over 2θ = 20°–70° with a step size of 0.02°, used to confirm phase purity of all three samples prior to neutron diffraction measurements.

Long exposure neutron diffraction patterns collected at the SAND facility using a Si-single crystal monochromator with wavelength 1.5656 Å, with powdered samples in a cylindrical vanadium can, used to determine crystallographic structural parameters of all three samples.
